newsitem.title: UK: Europe aluminium premiums tick up on trade buying.
newsitem.headline: Europe aluminium premiums tick up on trade buying.

text.p: End-user aluminium demand has continued at a low ebb in Europe but trade buying and low supplies of some material have pushed up physical premiums in Rotterdam, traders said.
"We're seeing quite good demand due to the trade mainly," one said.
Premiums in Rotterdam for Good Western duty unpaid metal have risen about $5 to $30/$40 from early October.
"There's not much in Rotterdam so what little there is people will ask more and more for. Most of it is getting shipped to the states or to the end consumer, not to Rotterdam," the trader added.
One trader, however, saw the market differently, saying producers in the Netherlands and Egypt had good stockpiles.
"They've all got stocks and all delighted to sell it."
Most traders said underlying demand was soft.

Many consumers regarded the recent futures strength as fund-led and therefore shortlived so were waiting for another dip, one said. Most players, however, expected higher economic growth to boost prices next year.
But traders are scrambling to buy off grades as supplies from Russia remain scarce, traders agreed.
"Everybody is looking for off grades, but not because they need it but because they are short of off grades and Russia has stopped producing them," one dealer said.
"Therefore you have the impression that there is really good business, business is booming. But it is not," he added.

Traders quoted a wide range of premiums for some off-grade material, with A6 metal, for instance, said by some to be at a $5 discount to LME while others placed it at a $13-$15 premium. In early October, traders pegged it level with LME to an $8 premium.
Traders agreed, however, that A0 was at a $20 to $25 discount to LME, compared to a $30 to $40 discount previously.
Now that Russia has taken strides in improving the quality of its metal, off-grades were being produced by smelters in Irkutsk, Tajikistan and Azerbaijan, traders said.
Irkutsk has had problems and is only able to produce A5, A6 and A0, but most of the output is going to China, they said.
A lot of the Azeri production was being sold regionally, with recent deals said to be with Iran and Iraq, one trader said.
In Europe, most of Russia's LME-grade A7E material is going to Liverpool, another trader said.
Most dealers said A7E was going for a $20/$30 premium, although one had it as low as $10/$15 and another at $35.
In the U.S. Midwest, premiums had firmed to $4.50 from $4.00-$4.25 earlier this month.
